strengths: The paper addresses an important limitation of stationary time-series causal discovery. Allowing individual variables to have different states, and representing their interactions through conditional summary graphs, is a useful contribution beyond a single global regime.

SDCI combines amortized graph inference, shared interaction functions, and learned state assignments in a coherent way. The connection to ACD and neural relational inference is acknowledged, and the combination is well motivated for datasets containing many sequences with shared dynamics.

The experiments provide positive evidence in several controlled settings. For example, Table 2 reports 97.08% summary-graph accuracy and 98.08% conditional-summary-graph accuracy for hidden-state linear data with two edge types. Experiments varying training-set size, variable count, and state count help characterize performance.

The NBA results demonstrate potential forecasting utility. The appendices also provide useful architectural, optimization, and simulation details and candidly acknowledge limitations of hidden-state recovery.
weaknesses: The comparisons do not adequately establish the advantage over methods suited to discrete regime changes. ACD assumes stationary structure, while the paper itself explains why the other evaluated discovery baselines are poorly matched to the simulations. Regime-PCMCI is discussed but not evaluated. A suitable regime-switching baseline and an ablation with comparable capacity would help separate the proposed contribution from the general benefit of allowing changing dynamics. Furthermore, SDCI learns shared mechanisms from 50,000 training sequences, whereas several baselines fit individual sequences, complicating attribution of the gains.

The identifiability argument needs stronger and more explicit assumptions. Theorem 1 omits the nonconstant-function condition used by Lemma 2. Appendix A.3 then infers dependence conditional on all other lagged variables directly from causal minimality, which establishes dependence conditional on the other parents; this extension needs an additional argument and appropriate support conditions. The treatment of conditioning on states should also specify when disturbance independence is preserved. These distribution-level results should be distinguished from guarantees for the learned VAE, whose consistency is explicitly left open.

The evidence for hidden-state discovery is narrower than the introduction suggests. The implemented state posterior depends only on the current observation, and Appendix F.2 explicitly reports failure with hidden history-dependent states, substituting observed-state supervision for scenario class 3. This limitation should be prominent in the main claims. Performance also deteriorates substantially in the less constrained three-edge linear setting, where conditional-summary-graph accuracy is 65.45%.

The principal quantitative evaluation for hidden-state springs measures only the union summary graph, although the proposed target is the conditional summary graph. Correctly recovering a union does not establish correct state-specific edges or switching behavior. Accuracy is also difficult to interpret when graph unions are dense. Reporting graph densities, a majority-class baseline, and state-aligned conditional or time-resolved precision and recall would substantially strengthen the evidence.

The NBA experiment supports prediction quality but does not establish causal correctness or show that causality explains the improvement. A comparable noncausal graph model would help isolate the source of the gains. The forecasting protocol should also specify whether forecast-time ball features and handcrafted states use ground-truth information or predicted trajectories, and how games are separated across training and testing.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the useful appendices. The manuscript does not clearly specify the state-network architecture, graph-prior settings, latent-label alignment for accuracy calculations, baseline threshold selection, or the number of training runs and meaning of error bars. Appendix C.2 additionally introduces an undefined lambda parameter. These omissions affect reconstruction of both the method and its reported comparisons.
